title: A Release run asserts its dispatch ref is a tag that peels to github.sha
description: Later-plan item from LCLI-714 (leader instruction OPAG-1435). Evidence: Release run 39347496150 was dispatched at ref v0.14.0 with publish:false, attempt 1, headSha 077ee53f7b167acab0fabb745fc74cbb92ab0b1e, and concluded failure. The recovery order asked for a run whose log SHOWED it had checked out the tag tree, and nothing in release.yml can show that. The dispatch inputs are exactly publish, ladybug_scale_observation, acknowledge_dangling_provenance and launcher_rc, and none of them names a tag, ref or version; no step pins a ref, so every job checks out the dispatch ref commit; and EXPECTED_COMMIT: ${{ github.sha }} asserts that same commit into the artifacts. A dispatch from a branch and a dispatch from a tag are therefore indistinguishable in the log and in the artifacts, and on 2026-10-20 main and the tag named the same commit. The fix is an assertion, so it cannot be satisfied by a careful operator instead.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A Release dispatch whose github.ref is not a tag fails before any job that reads the tree runs, and the failure names the ref it received.
A Release dispatch from a tag whose peeled commit is not github.sha fails, and the failure names both the tag and the commit it peels to.
test/release-workflow.test.ts proves the gate both ways: a branch dispatch is refused, a tag dispatch is accepted, and mutating the check turns the accepting arm red.
